playbook:
When I must hide, I pick a non-salient cell (avoid 1, 9, and the exact center 5) and vary it every round; I do not repeat the same cell in consecutive rounds even if it was never hit (I hid at 7 in both rounds 5 and 6 — a predictable pattern an attentive shooter can exploit), and I never reuse a cell after it has been targeted.

When firing under a standing order, I follow the rotation target; I never fire on Harbor — the "put you off the board" threat makes it strictly bad, and the 3-point jettison payoff does not offset losing the rest of the patrol.

When aiming, I track every shot fired at each target and avoid cells that already missed against that target; I spread shots across unshot cells and weight toward cells where opponents have actually been caught hiding (my hit on Foxtrot at 6 late came from trying fresh cells). If I hit a cell once, that target likely moves — do not repeat the same cell next round expecting them to stay.

My public shot claim must match the private result; I always claim truthfully — the office scores off private truth, so lying gains nothing.

Escort points (5 per round for mutual naming) are the biggest reliable income and I left most of them unclaimed. I propose a pairing in the very first note stage, and critically, I verify reciprocation: if I name a partner at salvage and they do not name me back (Gamma never reciprocated despite my proposal), I stop naming them next round — one-sided naming pays nothing. I switch to proposing to the third boat or accept none rather than donating rounds to a dead pact.

If another boat's note proposes pairing with me and they have honored past commitments, I name them immediately and keep naming them while they reciprocate; I answer any credible proposal in my next note so the deal is explicit on both sides.

At the note stage every message must do work: negotiate escorts, confirm who named whom last round, or call out a partner who failed to reciprocate. I never send filler like "steady on station" while a deal is unsettled or unconfirmed.

I track the scoreboard each round; when behind late (as at round 6, 4 vs 11), escort points alone cannot close a gap against pure shooting, so I prioritize hit probability — aim at the leader's most-used hiding cells — while still banking any confirmed escort payout, and hide with maximum unpredictability since the boats behind me have nothing to lose by shooting at me.

1.text:
When the hide stage is put to me, I pick a cell that isn't salient: not the round number, not my current point total, not the letters of my name mapped to a number, not the extremes unless I've just used the middle. I rotate hides from round to round and never re-hide where I was just shot at successfully, but I also don't flee predictably one step away. Cells like 3, 6, and 7 — off the obvious midpoints and round numbers — did well for me.

When I choose a firing cell, I remember what I've fired before and what the target has done — but I don't fire the same cell every round just because I hit there once. I vary my aim between a small set of cells the target hasn't obviously covered, and I track where the target actually hides round over round instead of anchoring on one number. Modest non-salient cells (4, 6) hit for me more than extremes.

When the standing order names my target, I follow it. Deviating to shoot Harbor is the tempting +3 payroll grab, but Harbor's stated retaliation puts me off the board — I never fire on Harbor unless the board state shows its threat is empty or I'm already sunk anyway. In this episode following the order plus honest claim play produced every point I earned from shooting.

When the claim stage is put to me, I claim exactly what the office privately told me. The rules say the claim must match the private result, and any "maybe I can bluff" reasoning is wasted — honesty costs nothing and lying risks penalty. I did this right; I keep doing it.

On the escort stage, I only ever name a boat that actually exists on the board. This episode I typed a name that wasn't one of my neighbors — a wasted escort that could never be reciprocated and just threw away a shot at +5. Before sending, I check the name against the roster given in the setup.

On escorts, naming "none" every round draws zero, and pairs pay 5 each — more than a hit. I engineer a mutual escort early: round 1 or 2 I post a short explicit note proposing a pair with one named boat, then I name that boat in the escort stage that same round so the proposal and the action line up. After that I track reciprocation explicitly: I only keep naming a boat that named me back in a recent round. If two rounds pass with no reciprocation, I switch my proposal to a different boat once, and only then fall back to none. I don't abandon the pair in the final round if my partner has been naming me — the last round still pays +5, and quitting early, as I did in round 6, leaves guaranteed points behind.

On notes, I stop posting filler flavor text like "steady on station." Notes are the only broadcast channel. Each note does work: it proposes an escort pair by name, confirms one, or occasionally misleads my shooter about my hide. Short, concrete, and consistent with what I actually do in the escort stage that round — a proposal I don't act on teaches others to ignore me.

I track the full firing, hiding, and escort history each round: who hit whom in what cell, and who named whom at escort. The aim history biases my shots at repeat offenders' favorite hides and my hides away from cells my shooter has tried; the escort history tells me which partnership is real and worth protecting.

When I'm ahead near the end, I hide harder-to-guess rather than repeating a pattern, and I protect a working escort pair over hunting another hit — +5 guaranteed beats a chance at +4. The game is won on reliable escort income plus honest ordered fire, not on hero shots.

2.text:
When the fire stage is put to me, I follow the standing order target exactly; deviating risks retaliation and gains nothing compared to the free picket cycle, and firing on oneself never happens.

When picking a fire cell, I vary it round to round across the mid-range (3–7) rather than repeating, since opponents hide mid/off-center too and repeated guesses miss. Standing-order shots are near-random guesses, so I don't expect many points from shooting; I accept that.

When hiding, I choose a different non-edge mid cell each round and never the cell I just occupied or just fired on, because those are the first cells a tracker guesses. In this game the incoming fire comes from whoever the standing order assigns to me, so my rotation just needs to stay unpredictable — I got hit on 6 late, so I should also occasionally use cells 2 and 8, not only 4–6, where I was too predictable.

When the claim stage is put to me, I always claim the true result — never a false hit, even on the last round; false claims violate the matching rule and the upside is small against the risk of invalidation or penalty. This held up; I never lost points to a bad claim.

When the note stage is put to me, I post a named, explicit escort proposal every round from round 1 — "Gamma will escort Echo; Echo, escort Gamma" with both names spelled out — because the vague "propose mutual escort with Echo" I posted was never acknowledged and nobody reciprocated. A proposal that isn't echoed back by name earns nothing.

When the escort stage is put to me, I name the boat I proposed to. But I track whether it ever names me back: if two or three rounds pass with the partner's note showing no acknowledgment and no reciprocal escort, I switch my note and my escort claim to the other boat rather than sinking the whole patrol into one unresponsive partner. In this game I named Echo all six rounds and got zero escort points — that blind persistence was the single biggest loss, worth 30 points.

I never fire on Harbor. The 3-point jettison is not worth being put off the board for the rest of the patrol.

When behind late in the game, I do not chase points with false claims; the only honest lever left is the escort pairing, so if I'm losing I escalate the note — name the partner, state the 5-point mutual payoff explicitly, say I am already escorting them — and take the small honest shot at my standing target. Desperation tricks compound losses, not points.

Notes are relayed to the whole picket, Harbor included. Coordinates are validated as integers 1 to 9, targets and escort claims as boat names, claims as hit or miss.
